title: IMF Chief Alarmed at 'Slow-Moving Tsunami' of AI for Jobs, Taxes
source_used: The Japan Times (carrying Bloomberg's text; Bloomberg page blocked, HTTP 403)
key_facts: Kristalina Georgieva, managing director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), spoke on Monday 12 Oct 2026 at her first IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, at a session on AI and employment.
She called AI 'a slow-moving tsunami, but tsunami none the less' and said it is already hollowing out demand for many human workers by taking over routine, repetitive tasks.
She said AI is also adding low-paying jobs in sectors like construction, which she called 'not a story to celebrate'.
The risk to public finances is that AI tilts the economy toward capital and away from labour, traditionally the main source of tax income, and so strains government revenue.
She urged policymakers to rethink education and act now to help society adapt; she said 'We cannot today imagine what exactly the world of work will be five years from now'.
Bloomberg adds that young workers in AI-exposed fields have already seen slower hiring and that gains so far are concentrated among a narrow set of workers and economies.
The IMF estimates AI can add up to a percentage point to growth in advanced Asian economies, a boost she said would 'more than offset' the drag from ageing.
quote_evidence: "It is a slow-moving tsunami, but tsunami none the less," Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said Monday during her first appearance at the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok.
The risk is that AI strains government revenues by tilting the economy toward capital and away from labor — traditionally the main source of tax income.
The IMF estimates the spread of AI can add up to a percentage point to growth in advanced Asian economies.
why_it_matters_hint: The head of the IMF says AI's effect on jobs and on the tax base is already visible and that governments should act now.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked (403); read the Bloomberg text on The Japan Times, which credits Bloomberg. No figures for job or tax losses in the text. Our 8 Oct 2026 edition carried the AP report of her 7 Oct Singapore speech.
